item.title: A more stable U.S.-China relationship matters for the world, says U.S. expert
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-02
A more stable U.S.-China relationship matters for the world, says U.S. expert NEW YORK, Oct. 2 (Xinhua) -- A more stable U.S.-China relationship has effects well beyond the bilateral relationship because the two countries are deeply connected to the global economy and play major roles in international institutions and global governance, a renowned U.S. expert on China affairs has said. In a written interview with Xinhua, Denis Simon, former senior adviser for China affairs to the president of Duke University, noted that Chinese President Xi Jinping said during the recent state visit to the United States that the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and making America great again can go hand in hand, complement each other and benefit the world. "I read this as an attempt to frame the relationship in terms of mutual national interests rather than as a zero-sum contest. Both China and the United States have their own national ambitions and domestic priorities, but those objectives do not necessarily require the other country to fail," said Simon, who also served as executive vice chancellor of Duke Kunshan University in 2015-2020. "Rather than asking either side to abandon its own national goals, the message is that China's development and America's prosperity can coexist and, under the right conditions, reinforce one another," he said. Regarding the constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability featuring cooperation as the mainstay, moderate competition, manageable differences and promises of peace, Simon described the formulation as "an effort to provide a practical framework for managing a relationship in which competition is unavoidable but conflict is not inevitable." "The key phrase for me is 'competition within bounds.' It recognizes that China and the United States will compete in areas such as technology, trade and strategic influence. The objective is not necessarily to eliminate that competition, but to establish boundaries so that competition does not become confrontation," he said. Simon said "manageable differences" acknowledges that some disagreements may be very difficult to resolve in the foreseeable future. A stable relationship, therefore, cannot depend on resolving every difference. "It needs mechanisms that allow the two sides to disagree without allowing individual disputes to destabilize the entire relationship," he said. "If implemented consistently, the framework could shift the emphasis from trying to eliminate competition toward making competition predictable and manageable, while expanding cooperation wherever interests genuinely overlap." Simon identified economic and trade issues as an obvious area where concrete progress could have immediate effects, while noting that technology and supply-chain questions are more difficult "because they involve both economic and national-security considerations." "But precisely for that reason, they require sustained dialogue and clearer communication," he said, adding that beyond bilateral issues, cooperation on climate, energy, public health and other transnational challenges could demonstrate that competition does not have to prevent practical collaboration. item.title: EU tightens migration chain as return rules approved
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-02
EU tightens migration chain as return rules approved This photo taken on Jan. 29, 2025 shows the Berlaymont Building, the European Commission headquarters, in Brussels, Belgium. (Xinhua/Meng Dingbo) Under the new Return Regulation, EU countries will operate under common return procedures, including a new European Return Order, and gain the option of establishing so-called "return hubs" in non-EU countries. BRUSSELS, Oct. 1 (Xinhua) -- The European Union (EU) member states on Thursday gave final approval to a new regulation to accelerate the return of people with no legal right to stay, adding an enforcement mechanism to migration and asylum rules that took effect in June. Under the new Return Regulation, EU countries will operate under common return procedures, including a new European Return Order, and gain the option of establishing so-called "return hubs" in non-EU countries. According to the EU figure, around two in three people ordered to leave the bloc currently do not actually depart. The regulation complements the EU Pact on Migration and Asylum, which took effect on June 12. The pact sets common rules for screening, asylum procedures, responsibility among member states and solidarity mechanisms, while the new regulation focuses on returning peoplefound to have no right to stay. The European Commission earlier described returns as the "missing piece" of the pact, while European Parliament rapporteur Malik Azmani called return the "final piece in Europe's migration system." PRESSURE FOR GREATER CONTROL The tougher return rules came after a turbulent summer that again pushed migration high up Europe's agenda. On July 30 and 31, tens of thousands of migrants crossed from Morocco into Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta, prompting Madrid to deploy the military and triggering calls from several European governments for tighter border controls. People gather on the Moroccan side of the border with Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta, preparing to cross into the enclave, on July 30, 2026. According to the Spanish government, at least 67 people died during the recent migrant crisis, while more than 48,000 of the nearly 50,000 migrants who entered Ceuta had returned to neighboring Morocco within 48 hours. (Photo by Liu Wenyong/Xinhua) The crisis came only weeks after the migration pact entered into application and added urgency to a broader push for tougher enforcement. Claire Kumar, head of policy and senior research fellow at ODI Europe, told Xinhua that public concern over irregular migration was strongly linked to a perceived "lack of control," with people expecting governments to demonstrate that borders and migration rules were effectively managed. That pressure has become politically significant as mainstream parties face sustained pressure from right-wing and far-right forces advocating stricter migration controls, she added. Pressure for further restrictions is also growing. Greece on Thursday proposed a mechanism that would allow EU countries to temporarily suspend asylum applications during large-scale arrivals deemed instrumentalized, with Germany, Austria, Denmark and Poland open to considering the idea. These discussions suggest that the adoption of the Return Regulation may not mark the end of the EU's tightening migration agenda. ENFORCEMENT MEETS REALITY Yet passing a common return law does not guarantee a sharp rise in actual returns. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez (C) observes the work of the Civil Guard in Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta, on July 31, 2026. (La Moncloa/Handout via Xinhua) The German Institute for International and Security Affairs (SWP) said in a recent analysis that return hubs are likely to remain limited in scale and heavily dependent on cooperation with third countries. It said that persistent obstacles include establishing migrants' identities, obtaining travel documents, securing cooperation from countries of origin, and finding third countries willing to host return facilities. Such problems cannot simply be bypassed by moving parts of the return process outside Europe. At the same time, Europe's aging economies still need migrant workers, Kumar said. She said that beneath increasingly restrictive political rhetoric, labor demand remains a powerful driver of migration. If adequate legal pathways are unavailable, workers may still fill those jobs through irregular or informal channels, increasing risks of exploitation and labor-market informality. The next test is implementation: whether the EU can turn its new legal powers into more effective returns while its aging economies continue to need migrant labor. item.title: 28 countries call for end to unilateral coercive measures at UN
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-02
28 countries call for end to unilateral coercive measures at UN UNITED NATIONS, Oct. 1 (Xinhua) -- China and 27 other countries, including Russia, Egypt and Iran, on Thursday called on the international community to end unilateral coercive measures, saying they interfere in other countries' internal affairs and undermine the foundation of multilateralism. History has proved that unilateral coercive measures are a major source of international turbulence and disorder, while developing countries and their peoples continue to bear the brunt of such measures, said Fu Cong, China's permanent representative to the United Nations, in a joint statement on behalf of 28 countries delivered at the Third Committee of the General Assembly. Unilateral coercive measures, compounded by secondary sanctions and over-compliance, have exacerbated existing humanitarian and economic challenges and threaten food, energy and financial security, Fu said. The growing use of tariffs as a tool of unilateral coercion has further politicized economic and trade issues, undermined the multilateral trading system, disrupted global industrial and supply chains, and impeded the efforts of the countries concerned to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals, he added. Moreover, unilateral coercive measures severely violate basic human rights, including the right to life, health, development and education, and impede the ability of targeted countries to realize those rights. The 28 countries call on a few Western countries to heed the just calls of the international community, honor their commitments to upholding the UN Charter and international law, and immediately, unconditionally and completely lift all unilateral coercive measures, said Fu. "We also call on member states, the UN system, and other international organizations to jointly oppose such unlawful practices and help targeted countries mitigate their plight," he said. item.title: China's high-speed rail network expansion to facilitate cross-city collaboration
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-02
China's high-speed rail network expansion to facilitate cross-city collaboration BEIJING, Oct. 1 (Xinhua) -- China's newly opened high-speed railway sections will help promote cross-city collaboration and closer regional economic ties, boosting the flow of talent, technology and capital across regions, experts said. On Monday, China opened four major high-speed railway sections spanning northern, northwestern, central and northeastern regions. This move further expands the world's largest high-speed rail network, enhancing connections between major cities, city clusters and key economic zones across the country. "The opening of the four lines will promote industrial transformation and upgrading and cross-regional industrial transfer, boost the development of resources along the routes, and inject new momentum into coordinated regional economic and social development," said Yuan Baohua, deputy director of the construction department of China State Railway Group Co., Ltd. Each of the four new sections helps bind regions closer together. The Xiong'an-Shangqiu section, for instance, tightens ties between Xiong'an New Area and central-southern Hebei, southwestern Shandong and eastern Henan, while the Harbin-Yichun line extends the two-hour transportation circle centered on Harbin in northeast China, Yuan said. As the rail network turns from isolated lines into an interconnected web, regional cooperation is deepening, according to Ma Botao with the China Railway Economic Planning and Research Institute. Ma said the expanding network is bringing cities and city clusters much closer together. Commuting within metropolitan areas now takes about one hour, living and working across city clusters about two hours, and business travel between neighboring city clusters and provincial capitals around three hours. "The railway network closely binds large and small cities, making industrial division of labor and cross-city employment the norm," he said. The benefits of the network extend beyond the areas directly along the new lines. For instance, the Yichang-Xingshan section narrows the time-space distance not just between the two cities, but between the Chengdu-Chongqing region and the city cluster in the middle reaches of the Yangtze River, Ma said. The new lines also provide direct support for key national strategies. Noting that the Xiong'an-Shangqiu section fills the gap in Xiong'an New Area's southbound high-speed rail corridor, Liu Yanhong, deputy general manager of Xiong'an high-speed railway corporation, said that the line facilitates commuting and business exchanges for relocated enterprises and institutions, and supports stronger industrial cooperation along the route. For cities newly connected to the network, seizing the opportunity depends on how well they position themselves. "Generally, large cities focus on research and development, finance and headquarters economy, while small cities should leverage their local agriculture, ecology, tourism and distinctive industrial strengths to undertake supporting manufacturing, agricultural product processing, and wellness and cultural tourism, serving as both industrial supporting bases and leisure backyards for central cities," Ma said. To turn transport advantages into real development gains, Ma advised cities to strengthen connections between high-speed rail stations and industrial parks as well as major population clusters, and improve housing and public services for talent. China is home to the world's largest high-speed rail network, with more than 50,000 km of high-speed rail in operation by the end of 2025. Under national plans, the network is projected to expand to 70,000 km by 2035, connecting major cities, city clusters and key economic zones throughout the country. item.title: China provides practical pathway for Global South countries to seize opportunities in AI development -- experts
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-02
China provides practical pathway for Global South countries to seize opportunities in AI development -- experts CAIRO, Oct. 1 (Xinhua) -- China's commitment to open source, openness, cooperation and sharing provides a practical pathway for Global South countries to seize opportunities in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) and bridge the North-South AI divide, experts have said. At the 2026 Global South Modernization Forum, held Wednesday in Cairo, participants said modernization in the Global South is at an important stage of overcoming development constraints, bridging capability gaps and transforming growth drivers, stressing the need to make good use of AI to strengthen endogenous development momentum. Former Egyptian Prime Minister Essam Sharaf said in his remarks that Global South countries face challenges related to resources, infrastructure and professional talent in developing AI. AI could deepen the Global South's external dependence on software, algorithms, data, computing power and knowledge, thereby creating a new North-South divide, he said. This requires Global South countries to strengthen cooperation, promote collaboration among research institutions and joint training, develop AI applications in local languages, and work together to build a responsible global AI governance system, Sharaf added. Chen Zhimin, vice president of Fudan University, said that "the focus of the Global South is shifting from whether these countries can access and use technology to whether they can truly transform technology into their own development capacity." These needs provide a clearer direction for deepening AI cooperation between China and Global South countries, he added. Ezzat Saad, director of the Egyptian Council for Foreign Affairs, said AI cooperation between China and Global South countries could help better align China's experience with the development needs and priorities of the Global South. Cai Fang, a member of the academic divisions of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, said China and other Global South countries face similar tasks in AI development, which makes experience sharing and mutual learning practically significant. The experts and scholars said Global South countries should take a more active part in discussions and cooperation on AI ethics, security, data governance and standard-setting, thereby promoting a more inclusive international AI governance system. Maged Botros, a political science professor at Capital University in Egypt, said AI development should take into account countries' different levels and stages of development and their specific needs. Gustavo Lema, director of communication and information at the Latin American Council of Social Sciences, said China's promotion of open-source AI models and encouragement of AI applications tailored to local needs could help more Global South countries use and develop related technologies. "Latin American countries have already begun using relevant Chinese technologies and tools to address climate change and improve production conditions, thereby better benefiting local people," he told Xinhua. At a parallel forum titled "Advancing Mutual Learning Among Civilizations Through the Proper Use of AI," Yang Bojiang, president of the Institute of Global Civilizations, said the deeper integration of technological development and civilizational dialogue could make AI an important technological infrastructure for promoting exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations in the new era. This could offer Global South countries a new path to modernization that both respects their cultural traditions and embraces the wave of modern technology, he added. Yang Cheng, executive dean of the Shanghai Academy of Global Governance and Area Studies at Shanghai International Studies University, told Xinhua that AI cooperation between China and Arab countries should move beyond "technological cooperation" toward "joint civilizational development," with AI governance rules drawing more on the ethical resources embedded in the traditions of both sides and cooperation helping promote exchanges and mutual learning between civilizations. AI is now being applied at an accelerating pace in specific sectors across the Global South. The Egypt-based African Disaster Mitigation Research Center and Fudan University have jointly developed intelligent optoelectronic remote-sensing technology and established a research platform for disaster monitoring and early warning to meet Africa's disaster prevention and mitigation needs. Mohamed ElGabry, director of the African Disaster Mitigation Research Center, told Xinhua that Chinese large AI models, characterized by open-source accessibility and inclusivity, provide more convenient technological conditions for Global South countries to leverage AI. Joseph Olivier Mendo'o, executive director of the international exchange department of the China-Africa Business Council, told Xinhua that during visits to rural areas in China, he had seen firsthand the application of AI in agriculture. "China seeks to demonstrate AI applications that can be adapted to local conditions. In the future, agriculture, healthcare and public services are expected to become important areas of China-Africa AI cooperation," he said. Held under the theme "The Rise of Artificial Intelligence: Opportunities and Challenges for Modernization in the Global South," the forum drew more than 100 experts and scholars from nearly 30 countries and regions. During the forum, "The Rise of the Global South: An Atlas of Academic Research on Modernization in the Global South" and "Top 10 Buzzwords in Global South Modernization Research of 2026" were released, and a session titled "Voices of Global South Youth" was held. A series of youth exchange activities and think-tank seminars were organized before and after the forum. Related Stories Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: China's Shenzhou-23 astronauts send National Day greetings from space station
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-02
China's Shenzhou-23 astronauts send National Day greetings from space station Chinese astronauts Zhu Yangzhu (C), Zhang Zhiyuan (R) and Li Jiaying, or Lai Ka-ying in Cantonese, for the upcoming Shenzhou-23 crewed spaceflight mission, meet the press at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, May 23, 2026. (Xinhua/Lian Zhen) BEIJING, Oct. 1 (Xinhua) -- The Shenzhou-23 astronauts aboard China's Tiangong space station sent video greetings to their motherland on Thursday, which is China's National Day and the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China. Commander Zhu Yangzhu and his crewmates Zhang Zhiyuan and Li Jiaying, or Lai Ka-ying in Cantonese, delivered their wishes for the country and its space program together as the station, about 400 km above Earth, flew over China. "When we look at Earth from the space station, that brilliantly lit land is the motherland we miss day and night," said Li, the first astronaut from the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region to travel to space. The three astronauts were launched aboard the Shenzhou-23 spaceship late on May 24 and have been in orbit for more than four months. They are in good condition, having completed in-orbit crew rotation with the Shenzhou-21 astronauts, repaired the station's solar panels in a spacewalk and deployed application payloads outside the station. This year marks the 70th anniversary of the founding of China's space program. Remarkable milestones include the launch of the country's first satellite, Dongfanghong-1, the BeiDou Navigation Satellite System that offers global services, the Chang'e lunar missions, the Tianwen-1 Mars mission, the Tiangong space station and the steady advance of crewed lunar exploration project. "We can never forget that in deserts, mountains and on islands, a group of people have gazed at the stars and kept striving, generation after generation, for 70 years, creating the glory of China's space program," said Zhang, who is on his first spaceflight. Zhu, from China's third batch of astronauts, is on his second spaceflight after the Shenzhou-16 mission in 2023, and is commanding a long-duration mission for the first time. "The 'baton of history' has been passed to us. We will certainly run this leg well, and keep safeguarding and building our home in space," he said. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. item.title: HKSAR celebrates National Day with fireworks, festivities
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-02
HKSAR celebrates National Day with fireworks, festivities Tourists watch the fireworks show celebrating the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China in Hong Kong, south China, Oct. 1, 2026. (Xinhua/Chen Duo) HONG KONG, Oct. 2 (Xinhua) -- On Thursday evening, both sides of the Victoria Harbour were teeming with crowds watching an eight-part fireworks show celebrating the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China. The 23-minute spectacle was a feast for the eyes and ears. With majestic music playing in the background, green and blue fireworks lit up the night sky in an ode to the country's mountains and rivers, while golden rings resembling intersecting orbits showcased the wonders of the cosmos. Awestruck crowds cheered while filming the show. Reluctant to leave, many of them lingered for a stroll or some more photos, basking in the jubilant mood. Tourists watch the fireworks show celebrating the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China in Hong Kong, south China, Oct. 1, 2026. (Xinhua/Chen Duo) The fireworks show was one episode of the day-long National Day celebrations, which started with a flag-raising ceremony and a reception hosted by the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) government in the morning. Noting that it was the first National Day celebrated since the announcement of Hong Kong's first five-year plan, HKSAR Chief Executive John Lee said at the reception that the plan provides a strategic roadmap for Hong Kong to seize the opportunities brought by national development by applying its unique advantages under "one country, two systems." "I am confident that as long as we, each dedicated to our respective roles, join hands and work in synergy with one another, Hong Kong will certainly be able to set out on a path to a brighter and more prosperous future," said Lee. The government of China's Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) holds a flag-raising ceremony to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China in south China's Hong Kong, Oct. 1, 2026. (Xinhua/Chen Duo) Also at the reception, Hong Kong's first astronaut Lai Ka-ying, who is now working as the payload specialist aboard Tiangong space station, said via video that she was extremely excited to celebrate the National Day in space, and deeply proud to be part of the country's manned space program. Districts across Hong Kong came up with their unique festivities, including a concert, a cheongsam ("long gown" in Cantonese) exhibition, and a food fair. The government of China's Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) holds a flag-raising ceremony to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China in south China's Hong Kong, Oct. 1, 2026. (Xinhua/Chen Duo) The Kai Tak Sports Park staged dance performances of Anhui Flower Drum Lantern, a national intangible cultural heritage item. Visitors also got a chance to learn and try Chinese knots and calligraphy there. Special treats also sweetened the National Day joy. On Thursday, residents and tourists can ride the tram for free, and watch movies at half price. Some public museums and parks opened for free, while 3,800 eateries offered discounts. item.title: Chinese celebrate 77 years of People's Republic, advance modernization with confidence
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-02
Chinese celebrate 77 years of People's Republic, advance modernization with confidence BEIJING, Oct. 1 (Xinhua) -- Hours before dawn on Thursday, Tian'anmen Square was already alive with anticipation. More than 100,000 people from across China gathered at the heart of Beijing to watch the national flag-raising ceremony as the People's Republic of China (PRC) marked its 77th founding anniversary. At around 6:10 a.m., the national anthem echoed across the square. People sang in unison, their eyes following the five-starred red flag as it rose into the sky. For many, the moment brought tears. When a large flock of white doves soared into the air, cheers and applause erupted from the crowd, filling the square with jubilation. Children waved national flags as they ran about, young people chatted and laughed with national flag stickers on their cheeks, and older visitors in bright, festive clothes smiled for group photos in front of an 18-meter-high flower basket at the center of the square. The festive mood extended far beyond the capital. Across the country, many streets were lined with national flags and floral displays, while residential communities were adorned with lanterns and traditional Chinese knots. "Every time I pass these flower displays, I feel inspired," said Gao Feng, a food delivery rider who crossed Chang'an Avenue, a major thoroughfare through central Beijing. "I truly believe that if everyone does their job well and takes things one step at a time, we can build a better future," Gao said. On Wednesday, Chinese President Xi Jinping and other senior leaders paid tribute to fallen heroes at a Martyrs' Day ceremony, honoring those who sacrificed their lives for the liberation of the Chinese people and the development of the PRC. China also presented the 2026 Chinese Government Friendship Award to 50 foreign experts in recognition of their contributions to China's development and to friendship and cooperation between China and other countries. Visitors take a selfie at Tian'anmen Square in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 1, 2026. (Xinhua/Yin Gang) REMARKABLE PROGRESS On this very day 77 years ago, the late Chinese leader Mao Zedong stood on Tian'anmen Rostrum and declared the birth of the PRC, marking a watershed moment in Chinese history. In the decades since, China has risen from a poor country to the world's second-largest economy and a major country striding toward the center of the world stage. By 2025, China's GDP had surpassed 140 trillion yuan (about 19.6 trillion U.S. dollars), accounting for about one-sixth of global GDP, while the country continued to contribute roughly 30 percent of global economic growth. Economic growth has translated into higher incomes and longer lives. Per capita disposable income rose from just 49.7 yuan in 1949 to 43,377 yuan in 2025, while average life expectancy more than doubled, from 35 years to 79.25 years. The country has eliminated absolute poverty and established the world's largest systems for education, social security and healthcare. Over the past decades, China has undergone one of the world's largest and fastest urbanization processes. Once largely agrarian, China is now home to about twice as many urban residents as rural residents. China has become a global manufacturing powerhouse, producing everything from new-energy vehicles to industrial robots and advanced chips. In 2025, output of new-energy vehicles exceeded 16 million units, while production of industrial robots and integrated circuits rose by 28 percent and 10.9 percent, respectively. It has emerged as one of the world's fastest-rising forces in innovation, making major advances in cutting-edge fields such as artificial intelligence, biomedicine and quantum technology. It has achieved breakthroughs in both land-based and sea-based rocket recovery technologies. These changes have also shaped the way China engages with the wider world. More people around the world are gaining a deeper appreciation of an increasingly innovative and culturally vibrant China through firsthand encounters. At the same time, its experience has broadened the paths for developing countries to achieve modernization. "We take immense pride in the extraordinary achievements of New China and have full confidence in the bright prospects of Chinese modernization," Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, said at a reception on the eve of the National Day. People watch a performance after attending a flag-raising ceremony at Dongfeng Square in Kunming, southwest China's Yunnan Province, Oct. 1, 2026. (Photo by Zheng Yi/Xinhua) JOURNEY AHEAD For visitors, the giant flower basket at the heart of Tian'anmen Square is a backdrop for holiday photos. And far more than that, it tells a story about where China is heading. This year marks the beginning of the 15th Five-Year Plan period, which runs from 2026 to 2030. The basket features 15 types of floral designs and five types of fruit, symbolizing hopes for abundant blossoms and fruitful results over the next five years. Beyond the flower basket, 10 three-dimensional flower installations line Chang'an Avenue, bringing themes such as new quality productive forces, harmony between people and nature, urban renewal and beautiful rural areas to life. Together, they highlight some of China's development priorities for the next five years. This photo taken on Oct. 1, 2026 shows a "flower basket" installation at Tian'anmen Square in Beijing, capital of China. (Xinhua/Yin Gang) Those priorities are backed by concrete goals. The plan aims to lay the groundwork for doubling per capita GDP from its 2020 level by 2035, while accelerating breakthroughs in core technologies in key fields. It also calls for raising average years of schooling among the working-age population to 11.7 years and life expectancy to 80 years, while further strengthening China's soft power. The 15th Five-Year Plan period represents a crucial window for laying a solid foundation toward China's 2035 goal of basically achieving socialist modernization and making decisive progress in that direction. The plan has dedicated sections on Hong Kong and Macao, outlining measures to support the two regions in better integrating into and contributing to the country's overall development. In September, Hong Kong unveiled its first Five-Year Plan, while Macao released its third in August, both aligned with the national development strategy. Since the beginning of this year, the Chinese economy has maintained progress despite pressure and achieved innovation-driven and high-quality development while demonstrating strong resilience and vitality, Xi said at Wednesday's reception. "As long as we remain confident, stay focused on our goals and move forward steadily, step by step, success will ultimately belong to the great CPC, the great Chinese people and the great PRC," Xi added. item.title: Xi calls for firm confidence, solid steps for China's national rejuvenation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-01
Xi calls for firm confidence, solid steps for China's national rejuvenation Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, delivers an important speech at a reception to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 30, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) BEIJING, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday called on the nation to forge ahead with firm confidence and take solid steps to achieve the great national rejuvenation. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a reception held at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China. China's National Day falls on Oct. 1. Li Qiang presided over the reception. Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang, Li Xi and Han Zheng attended the event along with around 800 guests. "The great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation is unstoppable," Xi said. "As long as we remain confident, stay focused on our goals and move forward steadily, step by step, success will ultimately belong to the great CPC, the great Chinese people and the great People's Republic of China." He noted that over the past 77 years, the Party has led the Chinese people in achieving two miracles: rapid economic growth and enduring social stability. "We take immense pride in the extraordinary achievements of New China and have full confidence in the bright prospects of Chinese modernization," he said. Since the beginning of this year, the Chinese economy has continued to progress despite mounting pressure and achieved innovation-driven and high-quality development, demonstrating strong resilience and vitality, he said. Efforts should be made to sustain this momentum, promote innovation-driven, high-quality and sound economic development, take practical steps to safeguard and improve people's livelihoods, and meet the targets and tasks set for the year, so as to ensure a good start to the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), he said. Xi stressed the need to remain firmly committed to the policy of "one country, two systems," under which the people of Hong Kong administer Hong Kong, the people of Macao administer Macao, and both regions enjoy a high degree of autonomy. He went on to say that the central government will support Hong Kong and Macao in integrating more fully into the country's overall development. The central government is committed to maintaining their long-term prosperity and stability, Xi added. He also called for efforts to deepen exchanges and cooperation across the Taiwan Strait, resolutely fight secessionist forces seeking "Taiwan independence," oppose external interference, and promote the peaceful development of cross-Strait relations to advance national reunification. China will stick to its independent foreign policy of peace, advance the implementation of the four major global initiatives it proposed, and promote the building of a community with a shared future for humanity to contribute greater certainty and positive energy to a turbulent world, Xi said.
